provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Ext family batch. Big-ticket licensed exterior remodel; copy names materials generically and never names a siding manufacturer. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Vinyl, fiber cement, engineered wood, cedar and metal siding compared by upkeep, look up close, impact and fire behaviour, and which suits which house
pageStructurePlus.why: Every siding conversation starts with 'vinyl or fiber cement'. That one answer sets the budget, so a page that answers it earns the estimate.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Body, trim and accent colour pairs on common house styles, lap versus board-and-batten versus shakes, and HOA colour approval notes
pageStructurePlus.why: Couples decide colour last and argue about it longest. Letting them try combinations at night keeps the decision on this site.

pageStructurePlus.contains: House wrap, window flashing, rotted sheathing, moisture stains, insulation board, and how hidden rot is priced once boards come off
pageStructurePlus.why: Hidden rot is the change order every homeowner fears. Explaining it before signing turns it from a surprise into a line on the quote.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Window and door casings, corner boards, frieze boards, wrapped versus PVC trim, soffit venting and the details that show a careful siding crew
pageStructurePlus.why: Cheap siding jobs show at the trim. Buyers comparing quotes judge the crew by the corners and casings, so show them close up.

pageStructurePlus.section: Living at home during a siding re-side
pageStructurePlus.contains: Which wall comes off first, how long each side takes, dumpster spot, window access, pets and kids, lead-safe practices on older painted siding
pageStructurePlus.why: The family stays home while the house is stripped. Knowing what each day looks like is what lets them pick a start date.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Cracked or blown-off panels, matching an older vinyl colour, when one wall gets re-sided to match, and what to photograph after a storm
pageStructurePlus.why: Many siding calls are a few broken panels after wind or hail. An honest page on matching wins the repair and often the full re-side later.

designDirections.name: Wall by Wall
designDirections.bestFor: Siding crews that win on a fast estimate for vinyl re-sides and storm repairs
designDirections.whyItFits: Cobalt on white and a clean grotesque read like a spec sheet. The page is the estimate form and the tap-to-call bar, nothing extra.

designDirections.name: New Face
designDirections.bestFor: Siding and trim contractors with before-and-after houses that show what a full re-side changes
designDirections.headlineSample: Siding and trim that make the house look new in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: The family's own combo. Evergreen and a refined serif calm a large purchase, and the before-after hero is the whole sales argument for siding.

designDirections.name: Exterior Stories
designDirections.bestFor: Design-led exterior remodelers selling fiber cement, cedar and full trim packages on older homes
designDirections.headlineSample: Whole-house exterior remodels, told house by house in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: A magazine serif and a vermilion accent suit long write-ups of one house at a time, which is how a premium exterior buyer reads.

openers.line: Your Google listing shows reviews and a number but no website. Someone pricing a full re-side wants to see whole houses you've sided before they let a stranger measure theirs.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: What a siding site behind that button looks like: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your listing's website link lands on Facebook. A homeowner weighing vinyl against fiber cement siding needs a comparison and an estimate form, which a feed can't hold.
openers.hook: Tap their Website link and confirm it lands on Facebook. Note the newest siding job there.
openers.linkLine: A siding page built for that comparison: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your siding site still has a free-host banner and a form that doesn't send. On a job this size, a dated site makes people wonder who stands behind the exterior warranty.
openers.hook: Open the site and look for a builder banner, an old copyright year or a dead form. Note which.
openers.linkLine: Same siding company, current and fast: {demo-link}

openers.line: On a phone, your siding gallery loads one house sideways and the menu covers the call button. Most exterior buyers browse from the couch on their phones.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note exactly what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your siding site, rebuilt for a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: The only way to ask you for a siding estimate is to call. A lot of people decide to re-side late at night and would rather send the address and the material they're leaning toward.
openers.hook: Check the listing, the social pages and any site for a form. If there's none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A siding estimate form that asks material, storeys and trim: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your before-and-after houses on Instagram are the best argument for new siding I've seen in {City}. They're lost in the feed instead of side by side on a page.
openers.hook: Pick two transformations on their grid you could name by material and colour. Mention one if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your siding transformations, side by side: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews mention trim corners done right and a siding crew that protected the flower beds. That's what someone comparing three exterior quotes needs to read, and it never leaves Google.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase about trim, cleanup or the finished look. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Those siding reviews next to the houses they describe: {demo-link}

openers.line: People plan exterior projects in late winter and book siding crews for spring. The ones they find in February are the ones with a full season.
openers.hook: Use this from January to early March. Name the month if they reply.

openers.line: After the last windstorm, a lot of houses in {City} have cracked or missing siding panels. Those owners search that night, and a voicemail sends them elsewhere.
openers.hook: Use within a few weeks of a reported wind or hail event. Call their number after hours and note if it hits a full or generic voicemail.
openers.linkLine: A storm siding repair request that works at night: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring siding installers. Good trim carpenters look at a company's finished exteriors before they apply, the same way buyers do.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note or a sign on the trailer. Note the date of the post.
openers.linkLine: A siding company page with a careers section: {demo-link}

openers.line: You side houses across {City} and nearby towns, but nothing tells a homeowner in {Neighborhood} you work there. 'Siding contractor' plus the town is what they type.
openers.hook: Find the towns they mention in posts or reviews. Use the one furthest from their address.
openers.linkLine: A siding page for each town you cover: {demo-link}

openers.line: If you offer payment plans on siding, that belongs on a page. A whole-house exterior is the number people want split into months before they invite a contractor in.
openers.hook: Only if they mention financing in a post, review or on the truck. Otherwise skip.
openers.linkLine: Siding financing explained before the estimate: {demo-link}

openers.line: Siding older homes means disturbing old paint, and your state licence is on the registry. A page that shows the licence, insurance and lead-safe practice answers the careful buyer first.
openers.hook: Check the state contractor registry and any lead-safe certification they mention. Note that a record exists; never quote a number you didn't see.
openers.linkLine: Licence and lead-safe practice on one siding page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Sounds like your siding work comes from neighbours who watched a house transform on their street. That runs out, and even those referrals search your name before calling.
openers.hook: Look for reviews like 'saw the house down the street' or 'neighbour recommended'. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Where a siding referral would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted is a sharp exterior, clean corners and straight courses. A house like that should be the first thing a stranger sees.
openers.hook: Pick the newest finished siding job on their grid and name it exactly: material, colour, profile, and the street if tagged.
openers.linkLine: That siding job, front and centre: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hey {Owner}, that {specific recent job} you posted is a sharp exterior, clean corner boards and straight courses.

I looked for siding contractors in {City} and found {Business Name} on social but no site with a material comparison or an estimate form. I put together a sample siding page to see how it would look, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Want me to send it?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, following up in case my message got buried. Here's the sample siding site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has a vinyl-versus-fiber-cement comparison, a page on what's behind the old siding, and an estimate form that asks material, storeys and trim. If it's not for you, say so and I'll leave you be.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for siding contractors here in {City}. I sent you a message a couple of days ago, did it come through?"

IF NO:
"Easy to miss. Short version: I built a sample siding site for {Business Name}, with a material comparison, a hidden-rot page and an estimate form, and marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I email you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range} depending on how many material and town pages you want, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and changes. For a siding company your size I'd quote about {Build Price}, a small slice of one re-side."
"Can I walk you through it for ten minutes this week, Tuesday or Thursday?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and a deposit invoice. We start the day it clears, and it's live before spring estimates."

objections.objection: My work comes from referrals and remodelers.
objections.handler: "Then your siding sells itself. A referral still searches your name before calling, and they want to see whole houses. The site is where the referral lands."

objections.objection: The manufacturer already lists me as an installer.
objections.handler: "Good, keep it. That listing sends them to search your name, and right now they find a Facebook page. Your own site is where they decide."

objections.objection: Siding is a big decision. People don't buy it online.
objections.handler: "Agreed, nobody buys a re-side from a web page. They decide who to invite over. The comparison and the before-and-afters are what get you on that short list."

objections.objection: Winter is slow and money's tight.
objections.handler: "That's when it's worth building. It's ready when people plan spring exterior projects, and the build is less than the materials on one wall."

objections.objection: I had a website guy. It did nothing.
objections.handler: "Most siding sites are a logo and a phone number. This one answers the questions you get on every estimate: material, colour, rot, how long. That's the difference."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}, because it's a comparison, a gallery, an estimate form and a few town pages. That's a fraction of one siding job."

email.subject: Siding site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "{Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for siding contractors in {City}, and I made a sample one for {Business Name} with a material comparison and an estimate form. I'll email the link. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner}, I'm taking the {Business Name} siding demo down on Friday to free up the space.

Want me to leave it up? One word either way is fine.
sequence.nurture:
Hey {Owner}, spring exterior season is a few weeks out and the siding estimates are about to start. Thought of you.

The site is still here, same price as before. {demo-link} if you want another look.

bullets: Peg the build to a small slice of one re-side, never to an hourly rate.
Price the before-and-after gallery by house count; one full transformation sells more siding than ten close-ups.
Material pages are separate lines; vinyl, fiber cement, engineered wood and cedar each answer a different search.
Quote the colour and profile picker only for contractors who sell colour choice, not single-colour vinyl crews.
Charge more for the estimate form when it asks material, storeys, trim scope and storm damage.
Expect a slower close than smaller exterior trades; send the scope in writing and follow up on the material page they liked.

lineItems.description: Max with an upkeep comparison, profile options and a gallery of finished houses in that material.

lineItems.item: Estimate form with material, storeys and trim fields
lineItems.description: Max with photo upload of each wall, storm-damage question and routing to two estimators.
Max when it covers several house styles, body-trim-accent combinations and a share link.

lineItems.item: Hidden rot and house wrap explainer
lineItems.description: Max with diagrams of flashing and wrap and a plain change-order explanation.
Max when it includes the homeowner's story, materials list and a slider for each side of the house.
Max when each town page shows finished siding jobs and local HOA or historic district notes.
Max when the comparison, estimate form and rot explainer are all translated.

whatElseYouSell.name: Whole-house exterior photo and video day
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A morning at your best re-sided houses, wide shots of every side and close-ups of the trim corners, fills the siding gallery and a year of posts."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, or the week a striking transformation is finished.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile posts for each siding job
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Every finished exterior goes on your Google profile with the material, the colour and the town, so the map listing looks as busy as you are."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 30, once the site is live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Review requests at the final siding walk
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "At the final walk, the homeowner gets a text asking for a review while they're still admiring the new siding. That's when they write the long ones."

whatElseYouSell.name: Jobsite yard sign and trailer artwork
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A re-side takes over a house for a week or two. A yard sign that says 'new siding by' with the site on it makes the whole street ask about their exterior."

whatElseYouSell.name: Street mailer around each finished exterior
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Houses on the same street were built the same year with the same siding. A mailer showing the neighbour's new exterior lands with people facing the same decision."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, once there are finished houses on the site.

whatElseYouSell.name: Late-winter exterior planning campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A February push with the colour picker and a spring start-date offer books siding crews before every other exterior contractor fills up."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in December, run in February.

whatElseYouSell.name: Siding storm-response page and ads
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Built once and switched on the week wind or hail hits, a storm siding page catches the panel-repair searches before out-of-town crews arrive."
whatElseYouSell.when: Build in the off-season, switch on after a storm report.

whatElseYouSell.name: Lookbook for realtors and remodel designers
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A printed and online siding lookbook puts your transformations in front of realtors prepping listings and designers planning exterior updates."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, once the gallery has several houses.

withoutAI.route: Window installers working the same walls
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Re-siding is the best time to swap windows, and you know the window installer who does it. Their site needs the same before-and-after logic as your siding."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Window and siding jobs are scheduled together. The siding client's introduction skips the cold pitch.

withoutAI.whoPays: The painter, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Customers who aren't ready to re-side still want fresh trim. The painter you send them to needs a site, and theirs sends siding leads back."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Two-way referral at the trim line, with no overlap in what each sells.

withoutAI.route: The siding and building supply yard
withoutAI.pitchLine: "You and plenty of other exterior crews pick up fiber cement and trim coil at the same yard. If you vouch for me there, I'll give that yard a page that sends homeowners to its siding installers."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Supply yards have real budgets and their contractor list is your next prospect list.

withoutAI.whoPays: The insulation contractor, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "When the siding comes off, walls are open for insulation. The contractor who blows in the walls needs a site too."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Open walls create a short window for insulation work; both trades gain from the referral.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "In historic districts, siding changes need approval. The consultants who file those packets need a clear site, and your finished exterior jobs are the examples they show."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Consultants and siding contractors meet on every historic job, and consultants buy credibility.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "Faded siding costs a seller at the first showing. Agents need a vendor page for pre-listing exterior fixes, with your siding company on it."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Agents recommend vendors for a living and pay for pages that make them look prepared.

withAI.route: Order assistant for the siding supply yard
withAI.pitchLine: "Contractors enter wall measurements and get a siding, trim and wrap order priced from your yard, with waste factors built in."
withAI.whyItWorks: It ties contractors to one yard's prices, worth more to the yard than a rebate.

withAI.pitchLine: "An assistant drafts the exterior change application from the house details and the district's siding rules, for the consultant to check."
withAI.whyItWorks: Approval packets are slow and repetitive. Faster packets mean faster siding starts.

withAI.pitchLine: "The window installer who works your siding jobs loses quotes to slow callbacks. Set up the follow-up texts for them in a week."
withAI.whyItWorks: Configuration of something you already built, with a warm introduction.

withAI.pitchLine: "Agents upload listing shots and get a rough list of exterior fixes, siding, trim and paint, with the local contractors to call."
withAI.whyItWorks: Agents want quick answers for sellers; the siding client is first on the list.

withAI.route: Energy audit summary assistant for insulation contractors
withAI.pitchLine: "Insulation contractors hand out dense audit reports. An assistant turns them into a plain one-page summary, with wall work flagged for re-siding season."
withAI.whyItWorks: Clear summaries close insulation jobs, and the wall work feeds back to the siding client.

withAI.pitchLine: "An assistant checks each siding colour and trim request against the HOA palette before the board meets."
withAI.whyItWorks: Rejected colours delay jobs by a month; managers pay to stop resubmissions.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back for siding estimates
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A missed call while you're on a scaffold turns into a text asking which walls and which siding material they're after, so your callback starts mid-conversation."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs their number forwarded and two approved lines of wording.

softwareAI.name: Siding cost estimator by wall area and material
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Homeowners pick house size, storeys and vinyl or fiber cement, and see a siding range before you visit. The ones who only wanted cheap vinyl sort themselves out."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their price per square by material, trim adders and minimum job.

softwareAI.name: Draw schedule invoicing for siding jobs
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Deposit at signing, a draw when the siding is delivered, the balance after the trim punch list, all sent on time with a card link."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their draw rules and payment account.

softwareAI.name: Thank-you replies for siding reviews
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A homeowner raves about their new exterior; a reply that mentions the colour and the trim detail they loved is drafted for you to send from the jobsite."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, with review requests. Needs a dozen past replies to match the voice. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Colour mock-up on the customer's own house
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Upload a shot of the house and it repaints the walls in the siding colour and profile they're choosing, so couples settle the exterior at the kitchen table."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their colour lines and a set of test houses. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer; mock-ups are labelled as previews.

softwareAI.name: Wall measurement draft from house photos
softwareAI.pitchLine: "From an aerial view and a few street shots it drafts siding squares, openings and trim lengths, so the estimator checks numbers instead of starting from a tape."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs past jobs with measured squares to check against. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Siding job board from estimate to punch list
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Estimates, colour approvals, material orders, start dates and trim punch lists for every siding job on one screen, not three notebooks."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, once estimate requests are steady. Needs their stages and who sells.

softwareAI.name: Change-order builder for hidden rot
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When the old siding comes off and the sheathing is soft, the crew snaps it, picks the repair and the homeowner signs the change order on the spot."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their rot repair prices and a sample change order.

softwareAI.name: Material delivery and dumpster scheduler
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Booking a siding start sets the material drop and dumpster for the morning before, and the homeowner gets a text about where to park."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their supplier and dumpster contacts.

softwareAI.name: Exterior warranty registry
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each siding job's materials, colours and workmanship terms on file, so a repair years later matches the right colour and the right paperwork."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs past jobs with materials and install dates.

softwareAI.name: Chatbot on siding materials and project timing
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Late at night it answers 'is fiber cement worth it here' and 'how long will my house be torn up', from your notes, and hands off anything it can't answer."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their material notes and current lead time. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Spoken walk-around to siding estimate
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Circle the house describing walls, trim and rot spots into the phone, and a siding estimate in your format is waiting when you sit in the truck."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their estimate template and pricing rules. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Storm repair colour-match lookup
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A searchable record of siding colours and profiles you've installed by street, so storm repair quotes start with the right match."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs past job records with colours.

softwareAI.name: Customer portal with colour sign-off
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The homeowner approves body and trim colours, sees the start date and which side the siding crew is on today, and stops calling the office."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs the job board running first.

softwareAI.name: Crew app with flashing and trim checklist
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Installers tick off wrap laps, window flashing, starter strip and corner trim with a shot each, so you see every exterior wall without driving over."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, once they run two siding crews. Needs their install checklist and a lead willing to test it.

softwareAI.name: Margin report by siding material
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See whether vinyl, fiber cement or engineered wood siding jobs actually paid once trim, rot repair and crew days are in."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs invoices and crew days for a season.

softwareAI.name: Spring re-side reminder to old estimates
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Everyone who got a siding estimate last year and didn't sign hears from you in February with the new colour picker and a spring start date."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their old estimate list.

softwareAI.name: Case study writer for finished exteriors
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each finished siding job becomes a short house story drafted from your notes: what was wrong, what went on, what it looks like now. You approve before it posts."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs job notes and approval on every story. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Historic district rule finder
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Type an address and it pulls the siding and trim rules for that historic district from the documents you load, so you know before quoting."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, for contractors working older neighbourhoods. Needs the district rule documents. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Siding installer applicant screener
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Applicants say whether they've hung fiber cement, run a brake for trim coil, and can get to the job, before you spend a call on them."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: When they post a hiring note. Needs their must-haves and pay range. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built a siding cost estimator for one contractor. Every exterior remodeler in the state answers 'how much for vinyl' all day."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The first siding client paid for the build and taught you the pricing logic.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Preferred-contractor portal for a siding maker
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your preferred siding installers need warranty registration, colour tools and a locator. I've built that for an installer already."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Manufacturers have channel budgets and the installer client proves you know the trade.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Contractor finder for a building supply chain
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A find-a-siding-contractor map on your site keeps the exterior contractors who buy from you loyal."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Suppliers spend on contractor loyalty already.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer member siding and exterior contractors a template with a material comparison and estimate form as a benefit."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations need renewal reasons, and one deal reaches many owners.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Agencies win the odd siding contractor and start blank. License my siding template with the rot page and colour picker done."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies own the relationship; you sell the finished part.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each siding territory needs town pages and an estimate form that routes to the right owner. Built once, rolled out to all."
"New-home buyers choose siding colour and trim upgrades in the design centre. An online exterior selector sells upgrades and routes to one installer."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Builders love upgrade revenue; the siding client becomes the default installer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Homeowners in historic districts don't know which siding changes need approval. A plain guide and request form saves the commission's staff time."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Commissions have small budgets for public guidance; the siding work gives you the expertise.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A short monthly note on where vinyl, fiber cement and trim prices are heading, built from price lists contractors share."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Built only from contributed data, it never claims more than the sheets show.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Storm siding page kit for wind-belt contractors
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A switch-on storm siding page, panel-repair form and colour-match request, ready for any siding contractor in hail or wind country."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Every storm-region siding company needs it the same week; selling a kit avoids custom work.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: A siding company in a new metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I work with one siding contractor per city. {City}'s taken; the next metro's best exterior crew is open."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Exclusive geography reuses the siding template and demo.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Someone started your siding site and stopped. I can finish it on an exterior template that's already live."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Stranded owners already decided to buy.

upsellLadder.offer: Whole-house exterior photo and video day

upsellLadder.offer: Siding cost estimator by wall area and material

upsellLadder.line: "A lot of your siding requests ask the same price question. The estimator answers it before you drive out."

upsellLadder.trigger: They mention an awkward conversation about rot found under old siding.
upsellLadder.line: "Next time the sheathing's soft, the homeowner sees the shot and signs on the spot."

upsellLadder.offer: Colour mock-up on the customer's own house
upsellLadder.trigger: A signed siding job stalls on colour choice.
upsellLadder.line: "That job waiting on a colour decision is why this exists. They see their own house in each siding colour."

upsellLadder.offer: Siding job board from estimate to punch list
upsellLadder.trigger: They mention a second siding crew or a backlog of several weeks.
upsellLadder.line: "Two siding crews and a backlog need one board. Let's get every exterior job on it."
